newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa launches unit trusts ahead of fx easing.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa launches unit trusts ahead of fx easing.

text.p: South Africa's Old Mutual said on Friday it was launching a range of international unit trusts to snap up business sprouting from the country's relaxation of some foreign exchange controls on July 1.
The government is set to allow individuals for the first time to invest up to 200,000 rand overseas.

Old Mutual said its international portfolio of trusts would allow South African residents to invest directly into a portfolio of U.S. dollar and sterling-based unit trusts designed to form a structured global portfolio.

Old Mutual International Holdings deputy chairman Garth Griffin said in a statement that key considerations in managing the trust would be effective asset allocation, stock selection and currency management in a broad range of global markets.
The trusts will invest in equities, fixed interest securities and cash deposits.

"The unit trusts cover a broad investment and risk spectrum, allowing clients to structure a portfolio which accommodates their profile in terms of investment objectives and capacity for risk," Griffin said.
Clients will have to invest a mimimum of 35,000 rand.
